MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and 23 producers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: 23 Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek business with Chinese importers and distributors at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Chinese customs data show Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldova's wine production is exported, and the EU now takes roughly 60% of its wine exports.

MARKET.head: Barossa's Sustainable Winegrowing Australia participation reaches 90% of vineyard area
MARKET.summ: Barossa Australia has revealed that more than 300 Barossa vineyards and wineries are now participating in Sustainable Winegrowing Australia, with over 80% achieving independent certification. 12,768 Ha (90%) of Barossa’s 14,162 Ha under-vine is participating in Sustainable Winegrowing Australia , a 1,264 hectare (10%) increase...
takeaways: Barossa Australia says 303 vineyards and wineries now belong to Sustainable Winegrowing Australia, up 66% in two years.
Participating vineyards cover 12,768 hectares, or 90% of the region's 14,162 hectares under vine, a 1,264 hectare rise.
Over 80% of members, 244 businesses, have reached best practice through third-party Freshcare audits.

MARKET.head: Australian wine small formats grow as moderation and single-person households rise
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22% to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39%, from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Single-person households are 26% of Australian households, up from 18% in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules restrict vague eco claims on wine labels and marketing
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, enforced from September 27, bans vague environmental claims like "eco-friendly" and unbacked sustainability badges on products sold in the EU.
Producers must substantiate claims with third-party certification or verifiable data, and old stock is not grandfathered in, so stickers are being used.
Fines for widespread violations can reach four percent of annual turnover, with enforcement left to each member state, creating varied national frameworks.

MARKET.head: Mark Harvey-Sutton named new CEO of Australian Grape & Wine
MARKET.summ: Australian Grape & Wine (AGW) has today announced the appointment of Mark Harvey-Sutton as its new CEO, bringing “extensive experience in industry leadership, agricultural trade and national advocacy” to the role. Harvey-Sutton has served as CEO of the Australian Livestock Exporters' Council since 2019, representing Australian...
takeaways: Australian Grape & Wine, the national wine industry body, has appointed Mark Harvey-Sutton as its new chief executive.
Harvey-Sutton has been CEO of the Australian Livestock Exporters' Council since 2019, handling international trade and market access.
He will start in the role on 13 January 2027.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of weekly fine wine trade as Burgundy share climbs
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded fine wine value, extending its lead, with 2019 and 2020 vintages top-traded.
Burgundy's share of traded value rose from 15.7% last week to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6%, with Soldera Case Basse and Sassicaia top-traded.

MARKET.head: India-EU trade deal cuts wine tariffs, but state rules still complicate entry
MARKET.summ: For years, India has occupied a peculiar position in the international wine industry: too large to ignore, too complicated to enter
takeaways: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement will cut India's 150% tariff on EU wine to 20% for premium and 30% for medium wines.
India imported 5.4 million litres of wine worth US$28.8 million in 2025, per Ministry of Commerce data.
Alcohol is regulated state by state, so distribution and licensing differ across Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru and Goa.

MARKET.head: German wine imports into China rise in volume, value and price
MARKET.summ: Imports rose in volume, value and average price in the first nine months, offering an encouraging backdrop for 45 wineries and importers heading to the German Pavilion
takeaways: China imported 4.23 million liters of bottled German wine in the first nine months of 2026, up 8% year on year.
Import value rose 11% to US$22.49 million, while the average import price increased 3%, per Chinese customs data.
Germany brings 45 wineries and importers to the national pavilion at ProWine Shanghai, running Nov. 10-12.

MARKET.head: California table grape supply to last through December for holiday promotions
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission says grapes will stay available in promotable volumes throughout December despite an early harvest.
Harvest is expected to conclude in mid-November, but significant volumes will keep shipping well beyond that point.
Commission president Ian LeMay cites consumer research showing 72% of grape buyers prefer U.S.-grown grapes over imports.

CULTURE.head: Sommeliers name underrated Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc picks beyond famous regions
CULTURE.summ: Though it has centuries of history in Burgundy, great quality Pinot Noir can now be found in every corner of the world, from the volcanic Otago peninsula in New Zealand to the high plateaus of Greece’s Amyndeon region. Across these different areas, Pinot Noir offers a wide variety of expressions, from dense, fruit-forward...
takeaways: Sixteen sommeliers were asked to name the most underrated Pinot Noir on the market right now.
Picks include Redbank Pinot Noir from King Valley, Australia, and Wasenhaus and Enderle & Moll from Germany's Baden region.
A separate survey of ten sommeliers named underrated Sauvignon Blanc, including Casa Jipi from Baja, Mexico, and Hannes Sabathi from Styria, Austria.

CULTURE.head: Napa consultant launches one-day human wine advice chat before Thanksgiving
CULTURE.summ: A new project empowers curious holiday drinkers to ask real experts for their advice
takeaways: Napa social media consultant Evan Roscoe launched Ask Wines, a 24-hour chat run by wine professionals.
The free service runs the day before Thanksgiving and invites anyone to ask questions about buying, selecting or pairing wine.
About 50 wine experts volunteered after Roscoe's Instagram poll, including sommeliers, winemakers, buyers and WSET students.

CULTURE.head: Gippsland Wine Show awards 85 medals from 116 entries, record Pinot and Chardonnay focus
CULTURE.summ: In a record medal tally, the 2026 Farmer’s Daughters Gippsland Wine Show attracted 116 entries “with a strong focus on the region’s famed Pinot Noir and Chardonnay classes”. Wine Gippsland president Rob Lightfoot said there was an “outstanding haul” of 85 medals from the 103 varietal entries yielding seven trophies, “a...
takeaways: The 2026 Farmer's Daughters Gippsland Wine Show received 116 entries and awarded 85 medals, including 15 gold, 31 silver and 39 bronze.
Gippsland Wine Company's 2025 Loch Chardonnay was named Best Wine of Show, with makers Mark Heath and Jane Taylor.
Dirty Three Wines' Marcus Satchell and Lisa Sartori took three of four golds in the Pinot Noir class of 29 entries.

CULTURE.head: Huntington Estate and Rosby lead 2026 Mudgee Wine Show trophy winners
CULTURE.summ: The 54th CCL Mudgee Wine Show has celebrated another year of outstanding wines and achievements across the Mudgee wine industry, with the 2026 trophy winners announced at the Mudgee Wine Show Awards at Di Lusso Estate on Thursday 10 September. Huntington Estate was among the standout performers, named Most Successful Exhibitor...
takeaways: The 54th CCL Mudgee Wine Show trophies were announced at Di Lusso Estate on 10 September 2026.
Huntington Estate was named Most Successful Exhibitor and its Tim Stevens was named Winemaker of the Year.
Rosby Wines took Best Wine of Show for its 2025 Riesling, while Heslop Wines won Best Red Wine of Show.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts how she came to wine, on Wine 101
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: VinePair's Wine 101 podcast, hosted by Keith Beavers, features Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wines.
In the episode, Story talks through her journey into the wine business in a casual conversation.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was due in Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain ranked sixth by value, below New Zealand, with only Chile's per-liter value lower among the top eight sources.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why I Enjoy Wine Competition Judging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Plus a guide to Le Puy wines - my notes from a recent vertical tasting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Writer is judging at the Asia Wine Trophy in Daejeon, South Korea, which has a dedicated panel for orange and amber wines.
A Georgian Khikhvi amber was rated in the mid-90s by all six judges, earning an instant grand gold without discussion.
Le Puy, a biodynamic right-bank Bordeaux estate of 54 hectares, left the Francs Côtes de Bordeaux appellation in 2017 and now bottles as Vin de France.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Traditional labels? Suck my duck
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Never say that wine labelling regulations are a subject devoid of humour. The Tribunal Correctionnel de Paris recently heard a case brought by anti-alcohol NGO Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over his provocative packaging. Vellas’s edgy cuvées have included “Little Fuck,” “Bad Angel” (its label...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Nicolas Vellas, a Languedoc vigneron, faces a Paris court case brought by Addictions France over provocative labels like "Suck my Duck" and "Punish Me".
Bordeaux has lost a fifth of its vineyard area in four years, with 30,000 ha set to be uprooted by end of December.
Bordeaux labels remain largely old-fashioned, featuring château pictures or family crests, while natural wine producers in less prestigious regions use bolder designs.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/1/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: The 2026 Harvest Is In , Here’s What It’s Already Telling Us About this Burgundy Wine Vintage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Early harvest data from the 2026 Burgundy vintage reveals exciting insights into the region's grapes, offering a first look at vine yields and pricing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Burgundy's Côte d'Or picking finished between 10 and 12 September 2026, after the region's earliest harvest on record.
The Comité des Vins de Bourgogne estimates Burgundy's 2026 volume about 30 per cent below the five-year average, with the official figure due mid-November.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Exploring the Roussillon (7) Château Nadal Hainaut
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Château Nadal Hainaut, an organic wine producer in the Roussillon making some nice wines. This visit was with Pauline Nadal,
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Château Nadal Hainaut in the Roussillon is an organic estate farming 27 hectares across 10 varieties, including a centenarian Carignan plot.
Pauline Nadal, a sixth-generation family member and trained ceramicist, is responsible for production at the estate.
The 2024 Domaine Nadal Hainaut Rosé de Syrah is scored 91/100, and the Signum 2020 Côtes du Roussillon, with 1800 bottles made, scores 94/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks dropping back on Sunday starts what she calls Kitchen Season.
Kitchen Season, she writes, spans November and December, when people feel a special itch to cook for others.
Maker's Table is sharing a list of kitchen tools the author uses year-round that become even more essential during festive cooking.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting Diaries: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Niagara’s Cabernet Franc harvest finally gets underway, plus the bottles that made my October memorable
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Buttonwood Grove's 2025 Blanc de Franc from the Finger Lakes is a white Cabernet Franc with about 10 g/L residual sugar, which the writer calls off-dry.
Château de Fosse Sèche's 2018 Éolithe VDF from Saumur is described as an early-drinking Cabernet Franc from silex de Brossay limestone, with 5+ years of life ahead.
Fogolar Wines' 2018 Cabernet Franc "Picone Vineyard" from VQA Vinemount Ridge, Niagara Peninsula, is called a serious, cellar-worthy Niagara Cabernet Franc.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family, ages its Albariño 'Mar' underwater in magnums off O Grove, Galicia.
The Mar is aged five months in the estuary's 13-16C waters, with the Standard Albariño made from the same wine.
Attis seals its underwater bottles with glass caps rather than cork, as cork was unreliable after waterproofing.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Yet Another Vintage Port Flex Post (Tasting Selections From 1985 - 2022)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Last week, I published a bunch of reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the (stellar) 2024 Port vintage. I typically follow those type of posts up with another post of other, older selections of vintage Ports that I tasted at the same event, and I offer them without much shame as simply […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude tasted older vintage Ports from 1985 to 2022 at an NYC media tasting, following up a post on the 2024 Port vintage.
The reviewer found the 2003 vintage Ports powerful and fruity, with one 2003 Port praised as his favorite of that vintage so far.
Several wines were judged too young to open, with the reviewer advising cellaring for another ten years for one.
